explanation: Correct. Minimal component: required input, destructured in setup, rendered in template with signal call syntax.
Invalid. In the template, text is a signal — it should be {text()} with the call. {text} would render the signal object, not its value.
Correct. Input with a default value, destructured in setup, rendered with signal call syntax in a text interpolation.
Correct. A model is a two-way binding — it's a writable signal, so calling .set() on it is valid. The template reads it with active().
Invalid. In the template, count is a signal — it should be {count()}, not {count}. The providers usage is fine though: inputs are hoisted and available there.
Correct. Directive with typed host, input, output, and host access in setup's second parameter.
Correct. :when conditionally applies the directive. It sits outside the directive's parentheses and cannot clash with input names.
Correct. The directive constrains its host to HTMLInputElement, has an optional input with a default, and accesses the host element reactively via afterRenderEffect.
Invalid. The same directive cannot be applied more than once to the same element. The compiler would reject this at build time.
Invalid. Derivations only support inputs — no outputs, no models. They have no DOM surface to emit from.
Correct. Derivation with two required inputs, returning a computed signal. No DI needed here, but the injection context is still available if needed.
Correct. @derive is used inside @for — each row gets an independent instance that follows the embedded view's lifecycle. Bindings are passed as named pairs.
Correct. Setup returns { template, expose } — the expose object becomes the public API available through ref<typeof TextBadge>(). Everything else stays private.
Correct. ref<typeof TextBadge>() gives a Signal<expose | undefined>. It's readable after afterNextRender, and .text() is the exposed readonly signal.
Invalid. Refs are readable only after afterNextRender — accessing them synchronously in setup will always yield undefined. The read must happen inside afterNextRender or in a reactive context.
Correct. Directive expose is captured with :ref={variable} on the use: binding. The tooltip directive exposes a toggle() method, accessed through the ref signal.
Correct. refMany collects multiple component instances into a Signal<expose[]>. Each TextBadge ref={items} contributes to the same collection.
Invalid. Both 'children' and 'ref' are reserved names at the component level — they cannot be declared as component bindings.
Invalid. 'children' is a reserved name — it's provided by Angular from nested content and cannot be declared as a binding. The 'header' fragment is fine.
Correct. Named fragment with typed parameter, rendered inside @for with the item passed as argument.
Invalid (likely). use: directives on components only work if the component uses component.proxy<T>. A plain component() doesn't expose a native element surface for directives.
Correct. component.proxy<HTMLButtonElement> exposes a native button surface. Directives applied to <IconButton /> will be forwarded to the inner <button> via @forward().
Correct. component.wrap forwards remaining bindings of Inner. The wrapper adds its own 'extra' input and places @forward() on the inner component.
Invalid. The token has no factory — the provide(token) shorthand requires the token to have a factory defined. Without one, you must use provide(token, () => 'value') with an explicit factory.
Correct. With autoProvided: true, the token is registered at root scope automatically — no need for provide() in the component's providers array.
Correct. Inputs are hoisted and available in providers before setup runs. The factory has injection context.
